summary: Atlassian development involves creating app descriptors or OAuth integrations. While private apps are easy to start, public listing requires rigorous partner enrollment, due diligence, and a formal review process. New Connect apps cannot be published to the Marketplace.

reason.text: The claims describe a straightforward process of creating an app descriptor file and a static HTML page to begin development.

access_ladder.name: Private Development
access_ladder.allows: The app is restricted to the developer's own account for installation and usage.

claims.text: When you create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app, it's private by default. This means that only you can install and use it.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: When you create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app, it's private by default. This means that only you can install and use it.

access_ladder.name: Shared Distribution
access_ladder.allows: The developer can distribute the app to other users by enabling sharing.

claims.text: If you want to distribute your app to other users, you must enable sharing.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: If you want to distribute your app to other users, you must enable sharing.

access_ladder.name: Marketplace Listing
access_ladder.allows: The app can be listed on the Atlassian Marketplace with informational details.

claims.text: Although OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps can be listed on the Atlassian Marketplace, they will appear as informational listings only, with limited Marketplace features.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Although OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps can be listed on the Atlassian Marketplace, they will appear as informational listings only, with limited Marketplace features.

claim.text: You must create an OAuth 2.0 integration in the developer console to create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: In the Developer console, select the Create dropdown and choose OAuth 2.0 integration to create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.

claim.text: A build number is mandatory for the Marketplace app.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Build number - the unique identifier for each build, which determines the order of different versions of the Marketplace app. This field is mandatory.

claim.text: You must provide access to a test instance of your software for the review team.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: In order to test the integration we will need access to a test instance of your software so we can run through the set up and configuration.

claim.text: All new publicly listed apps must be approved by Atlassian.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: All new publicly listed apps need to be approved by Atlassian.

go_public.item: Privacy and security tab and ticket approval

claim.text: Partners must have a privacy and security tab and ticket approval.

claim.evidence_quote: Privacy and security tab and ticket approval

claim.text: Partners must have a partner verification ticket.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Partner verification ticket

claim.text: Partners must accept the Marketplace Partner Agreement upon submission.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Upon submission, accept the Marketplace Partner Agreement.

claim.text: Partners must create a privacy policy.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Create a privacy policy

claim.text: At least one contact from the partner profile must be registered with the Atlassian Developer Community.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: At least one contact from your partner profile is registered with the Atlassian Developer Community for future correspondence.

claim.text: Per-tenant rate limits are capped at 500,000 points per hour.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Per-tenant rate limits are capped at 500,000 points per hour for Standard, Premium, and Enterprise editions.

claim.text: The default burst limit for GET requests is 100 requests per second.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: HTTP method Requests per second GET 100

blockers.issue: The app descriptor file can only be fetched from specific web server ports.
blockers.fix: Ensure the web server is running on port 80, 443, or 8080.

claim.text: The app descriptor file can only be fetched from specific web server ports.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: The descriptor file can only be fetched from web server ports 80, 443, or 8080.

blockers.issue: New Connect apps cannot be published to the Atlassian Marketplace.
blockers.fix: Use Forge for new app development.

claim.text: New Connect apps cannot be published to the Atlassian Marketplace.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote:
You can no longer publish Connect apps on the Atlassian Marketplace. All new extensibility features
will be delivered only on Forge.

claim.text: You cannot delete an app if it is currently installed on a site.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: You can only delete an app if it's not installed anywhere. If your app is currently installed on a site, uninstall it.

claim.text: The implicit grant flow is not supported.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) currently supports the code grant flow only. It does not support the implicit grant flow.

blockers.issue: The App Key cannot be changed after it is set.
blockers.fix: Choose the App Key carefully as it is permanent.

claim.text: The App Key cannot be changed after it is set.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: App Key - the unique identifier for the Marketplace app. This value can't be altered once you set it.

blockers.issue: Incomplete listing fields, missing policy links, or install failures on a clean site…
blockers.fix: Review app approval guidelines one final time and test your app on a clean environment one final time.

claim.text: Incomplete listing fields, missing policy links, or install failures on a clean site cause review rejections.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Most review rejections come from avoidable gaps like incomplete listing fields, missing policy links, or install failures on a clean site.

claim.text: Apps that break the host Atlassian app UI will be rejected.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: If the UI breaks, your app will be rejected.

claim.text: Trademark infringement results in automatic rejection.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Trademark infringement is an automatic rejection, so be sure to read our brand guidelines for Marketplace Partners before submitting your app.

claim.text: Basic authentication is not permitted for public, approved apps.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Whilst your app may make use of Basic authentication with Atlassian's product REST APIs for ease of development/speed during development, this shall not be the case for any public, approved app.

blockers.issue: Do not use prohibited words in your app name.
blockers.fix: Remove prohibited words from the app name.

claim.text: Do not use prohibited words in your app name.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Prohibited words: Do not use "Atlassian," "plugin," "beta," "add-on," or "app."

blockers.issue: Do not start your app name with an Atlassian product name.
blockers.fix: Reorder the app name so the Atlassian product name is not at the start.

claim.text: Do not start your app name with an Atlassian product name.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Branding: Do not start with an Atlassian product name. Use "Time Tracker for Jira," not "Jira Time Tracker."

claims.text: You can choose between account-level or resource-level grant types when creating an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: When you create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app, you can choose between two grant types: Account-level grant: The user’s consent applies at the Atlassian account level. A single grant can cover access to multiple sites where your app is installed, subject to the scopes you request. Resource-level grant: The user’s consent is limited to the specific site(s) they select on the consent screen.
